Broadcasting refers to the distribution of video and audio content to a dispersed audience through electronic media such as television, radio, or the internet, where one source transmits to many receivers simultaneously.

A peripheral is added to a host computer's hardware to expand its abilities. Peripherals include input devices (keyboard, mouse), output devices (monitor, printer), and storage devices (USB drives, external hard disks).
A laptop computer features a Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) screen. Laptops use flat LCD panels because they are thin, lightweight, and energy-efficient, making them suitable for portable computing.

Charles Babbage invented both the Difference Engine (1822) and the Analytical Engine (1837). These mechanical computing machines pioneered the concepts of programmable computation, earning Babbage the title 'Father of the Computer'.

A program is a set of instructions that directs a computer in performing a specific task. Programs (software) tell the computer's hardware what operations to perform, in what sequence, and with what data.

Quantitative data (numeric data) can exist in two forms: continuous (can take any value within a range, e.g., height, temperature) and discrete (can only take specific distinct values, e.g., number of students).

Copyright law protects the expression of ideas, not the ideas themselves. For example, a novel, painting, or piece of music is protected — but the underlying concept or plot idea cannot be copyrighted.

Supercomputers can process billions (or even trillions) of operations per second. They are used for complex scientific simulations, weather forecasting, and research. They are very expensive and not affordable for homes.
A bus is a collection of wires (communication pathways) through which data is transmitted from one part of the computer to another. Types include the data bus, address bus, and control bus.

The primary memory of a computer is divided into RAM (Random Access Memory) and ROM (Read Only Memory). RAM is volatile (loses data when powered off); ROM is non-volatile (retains data). Together they constitute primary (main) memory.

Data is defined as a collection of unorganised raw facts and figures. It has no meaning on its own until it is processed and interpreted — at which point it becomes information.

Software is the set of programs, routines, and procedures used to operate and manage computer hardware. It includes system software (operating systems, translators) and application software (word processors, games).
